normative_extracts.spec_section: web.dev: Rendering on the Web (Hydration Cost)
normative_extracts.quote: Hydration requires downloading, parsing, and executing component JavaScript on the client to attach event listeners and reconstruct state over server-rendered HTML.
Resumability serializes application state, component boundaries, and event listener closures into HTML attributes so execution resumes on interaction without eager boot.

browser_support.notes: Architectural pattern supported in all browsers; framework primitives (Qwik resumability, React Server Components + selective hydration) vary in maturity.

engine_internals.mechanism_summary: Eliminates eager O(N) hydration boot by serializing framework state into HTML and lazily loading only the clicked handler's JS chunk via event delegation.

production_failures.symptom: Page appears interactive at 1.2s (FCP) but clicks do nothing for 2.5s (Uncanny Valley)
production_failures.root_cause: SSR painted the button HTML early, while eager hydration blocked the main thread downloading and executing the entire component tree.
production_failures.mitigation: Use selective/partial hydration (Islands), React Server Components, or resumable lazy handlers to keep main-thread boot under 50ms.

production_failures.symptom: Hydration mismatch error wipes and re-renders the entire SSR DOM on the client
production_failures.root_cause: Client render produced different HTML than SSR (e.g., reading window.innerWidth or new Date() during initial render).
production_failures.mitigation: Keep initial render deterministic across server and client, deferring browser-only values to post-mount effects.
